title: Battle of the Ancients - A Look at the Demo Version
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRlM9dhgPTg

A tactical skirmish game is not Daniel (@dungeondive)'s natural habitat, and he says so in the first minute. He is here for three reasons: Robert Lemon's art, which he rates among the boldest in the industry; the Dark Venture world, a science-fantasy setting he finds genuinely rare on a game shelf; and the fact that Battle of the Ancients can be played solo against an AI.

The demo box holds four asymmetric factions — the Vorpin, who mutate themselves stronger; the Bomark, who split, fuse and absorb the dead; the Orpal, who portal minions in through rift tokens; and the Dargon, who grow replacements from eggs. Units carry an S and a D value, the number of d6 they roll attacking or defending. Highest roll wins, and the winner may kill, capture or absorb.

The scenario he walks through has him barricading a ruined laboratory against a pair of wolves while a hungry Bomark wakes nearby — a small puzzle with a story attached, which is exactly the hook. Six action dice drive every turn, and a genetic memory card lets you bank up to three unused faces for later.

Daniel is candid that asymmetric balance is outside his wheelhouse, and predicts the usual fortnightly forum reversals about who is overpowered. What he wants is the narrative scenarios, played on this small quadrant rather than the full map.

----

Narrative scenarios turned a skirmish game into something Daniel actually wanted to play. What genre do you only enjoy once someone bolts a story onto it?
